identity.title: Atomic OAuth Stage B Terminal-Journal Publication Repair
identity.objective: Replace non-atomic OAuth Stage B terminal-journal publication with a complete fsynced same-directory temporary write and atomic no-overwrite publication, preserving single reservation, one dispatch maximum, no retry, replay verification and fail-closed interrupted writes; no provider call.

scope.rollback_surface: Revert the single repair commit; the OAuth module returns to direct exclusive-create terminal publication. No journal, credential or store format changes.

api_matrix.reason: One internal journal publication step changes; public API, record schema and statuses are unchanged.

items.before: Terminal JSON created with exclusive open then written; a concurrent reader could parse an empty or partial file and return JOURNAL_INVALID.
items.after: Terminal bytes are written and fsynced to a same-directory temporary file and hard-linked into place atomically without overwrite; readers see no terminal or the complete one.
items.compatibility_requirement: Same terminal path, bytes, record identity and status values; reservation marker unchanged; an interrupted write leaves only the reservation and never allows a second dispatch.

items.required_rule: Terminal published complete or not at all; never overwritten; no torn read by concurrent callers
items.validation_rule: Terminal published complete or not at all; never overwritten; no torn read by concurrent callers

items.required_rule: Exclusive reservation before dispatch; at most one dispatch; interrupted publication blocks further dispatch; corrupted completed journal stays JOURNAL_INVALID
items.validation_rule: Exclusive reservation before dispatch; at most one dispatch; interrupted publication blocks further dispatch; corrupted completed journal stays JOURNAL_INVALID

identity_derivations.reason: The WP introduces no new authoritative domain identities; source IDs remain native, and the noncanonical scratch manifest uses a locally checked SHA-256 checksum only.

state_transitions.reason: Use exact required repository governance transition chain.

items.condition: Native RUNTIME prompt/spec/readiness passes on the exact five-path scope with no unresolved source contradictions.
Karl expressly authorizes this targeted repair WP/PR; never provider, OAuth, credential, network or trading activity.
Atomic publication fix plus deterministic concurrency regression, focused tests, native readiness, stable-head full suite and hosted CI on one PR; no merge.

failure_precedence.reason: Use unchanged repository-native readiness-failure order; runtime decision failures are sanitized, local-only and never provide authority.

examples.reason: No new domain validation schema introduced; seven named focused negative-control tests cover required semantics and adversarial cases.

evidence_plan.reason: Two observable requirements mapped to named tests, plus readiness, guards, one stable-head full suite and hosted CI.

items.expected_result: A reader concurrent with a writer paused after fsync sees no terminal and gets ATTEMPT_ALREADY_RESERVED, never JOURNAL_INVALID; publication never overwrites; a crash before publication leaves no terminal and blocks redispatch; exactly one dispatch.

Existing matrix still holds: one dispatch per journal, cold replay with zero redispatch, interrupted reservation blocked, tampered terminal JOURNAL_INVALID, six concurrent callers produce exactly one dispatch and only VALID_OUTPUT or ATTEMPT_ALREADY_RESERVED.

forbidden_in_this_wp: Any real OAuth, ChatGPT, Codex or provider call, credential or token read, or reuse of the PR243 consumed journal.
Any change to reservation semantics, dispatch count, retry, fallback, record schema, statuses or AUTO-01 admission.
Any market, account or product network, order, capital, scheduler or live activation.
Any edit outside the five named paths, including PR #244 files, dependencies, workflows or historical guards.
